title: India, 1920
tagline: Non-co-operation, new national universities and the first all-India labour federation.

morningRoutine.detail: Common rice sold retail at about Rs 7.5 a maund in Bombay and Rs 12.5 in Delhi in 1920, near the top of a run of dear years after the war.

morningRoutine.detail: Gandhi edited the English weekly Young India, published from 1919 to 1931.
Within weeks in autumn 1920 Aligarh Muslim University, Gujarat Vidyapith and other national institutions were founded as part of the non-co-operation programme.
The All India Trade Union Congress was founded in Bombay in October 1920 with Lala Lajpat Rai as its first president.

technology.name: Tata hydroelectric power
technology.description: The Tata hydroelectric company commissioned its Khopoli plant in 1915 and a second at Bhivpuri in 1919, bringing hydro power from the Western Ghats to Bombay.

technology.name: Steel at Jamshedpur
technology.description: The Tata Iron and Steel Company began producing pig iron in 1911 and steel in 1912 at Jamshedpur, and kept working through the First World War.

technology.name: The Saha ionisation equation
technology.description: Meghnad Saha's work on the thermal ionisation of elements produced the equation, dated about 1920, that lets astronomers relate a star's spectrum to its temperature.

technology.name: Raman and the Calcutta laboratories
technology.description: C. V. Raman became the first Palit Professor of Physics at the University of Calcutta in 1917, and research scholars from several universities worked under him at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science.

technology.name: Gateway of India (building)
technology.description: The arch at Bombay's waterfront was begun in 1913 and completed in 1924, to commemorate George V's landing in 1911.
